results.name: participant_alternation_pref_sd
results.description: Across-participant SD of each person's rate of choosing the more-alternating sequence (trials whose alternation counts differ); observed > null means the single-population model under-produces individual differences in alternation preference.

results.name: high_alternation_preference
results.description: Among trials where both sequences have alternation proportion >= 0.5 and differ in alternation count, the rate of choosing the more-alternating one; observed > null means humans prefer heavier alternation than the model's fitted alternation prototype allows, observed < null means the model over-rewards alternation at the high end.

results.name: alternation_pref_drift_over_trials
results.description: Rate of choosing the more-alternating sequence in the second half of each session minus the first half; positive observed vs null means preferences drift toward alternation over the session, which the static model cannot produce.

results.name: pair_choice_extremity
results.description: Mean over distinct (unordered) pairs of |share choosing the lexicographically smaller sequence - 0.5|; observed > null means the model's pair predictions are too weak (humans more unanimous), observed < null means the model is overconfident.
results.code:
# name: pair_choice_extremity
# description: Mean over distinct (unordered) pairs of |share choosing the lexicographically smaller sequence - 0.5|; observed > null means the model's pair predictions are too weak (humans more unanimous), observed < null means the model is overconfident.
def test_statistic(df):
    a = df["sequence_a"].to_numpy(); b = df["sequence_b"].to_numpy()
    first = np.where(a < b, a, b); second = np.where(a < b, b, a)
    chose_first = np.where(a < b, df["chose_left"].to_numpy(), 1 - df["chose_left"].to_numpy())
    key = pd.Series(first) + "|" + pd.Series(second)
    r = pd.Series(chose_first).groupby(key.to_numpy()).mean()
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(r.to_numpy() - 0.5)))

results.name: shorter_run_rate_matched_alternations
results.description: Among trials whose two sequences have equal alternation counts but different longest-run lengths, the rate of choosing the sequence with the shorter longest run; observed > null means the model under-weights long streaks as a cue to non-randomness.

results.name: balance_rate_matched_alternations
results.description: Among trials whose sequences have equal alternation counts but different global |#H-#T|, the rate of choosing the globally more balanced sequence; observed > null means the model under-weights global H/T balance (its multiscale averaging dilutes it), observed < null means it over-weights it.

results.name: same_side_perseveration
results.description: Rate at which a participant chooses the same screen side (left/right) as on their previous trial; observed > null means response-side perseveration the trial-independent model does not produce, observed < null means excess side switching.

results.name: perfect_alternation_choice_rate
results.description: Rate of choosing a perfectly alternating sequence (HTHT.../THTH...) when it is paired with a non-perfectly-alternating one; observed > null means the model under-predicts acceptance of the extreme over-alternating pattern, observed < null means it over-predicts it.
